column1: #mapping_set_description: "Mappings from the terms of xAPI 2.0 (IEEE 9274.1.1-2023) — Statement data model (https://foxxi-bridge.interego.xwisee.com/ns/xapi) to other vocabularies: one row for each SKOS mapping the ontology makes, generated from it. The ontology is aligned term by term to https://w3id.org/xapi/ontology; each of its 44 terms with no counterpart there is listed as mapped to sssom:NoTermFound. The mappings into it, and the reasons a match is broad or close, are to it as it was at 2017-08-11 (object_source_version); what it declares there, and its axioms, are recorded at https://github.com/markjspivey-xwisee/interego/blob/foxxi-ns-2026.10.1/applications/foxxi-content-intelligence/src/spec/adl-xapi-ontology.ts."
#comment: "Independent formalization by Mark Spivey (Foxxi Mediums Inc.). Not affiliated with or endorsed by IEEE or ADL. Where this document and the published standard differ, the standard governs."

column11: Broader there: ADL's ontology places Activity Definitions and activity types (xapi:ActivityDefinition, and under it xapi:ActivityType) under xapi:Activity by rdfs:subClassOf, so its instances include them; here an Activity's definition and its type are not Activities.

Broader there: ADL's ontology places activity types (xapi:ActivityType) under xapi:ActivityDefinition by rdfs:subClassOf, so its instances include them; here an activity type is not an Activity Definition. ADL's ontology also labels the class Activity, the label of its Activity class; it is the Activity Definition.
Broader there: ADL's ontology places Accounts (xapi:Account) under xapi:Actor by rdfs:subClassOf, so its instances include them; here an Account is not an Actor.

Broader there: ADL's ontology places attachment usage types (xapi:AttachmentUsageType) under xapi:Attachments by rdfs:subClassOf, so its instances include them; here an Attachment's usage type is not an Attachment. ADL names the class in the plural, after the Statement's attachments property; its instances are the Attachment objects.

Broader there: ADL's ontology places context activities (xapi:ContextActivities) under xapi:Context by rdfs:subClassOf, so its instances include them; here a Context's context activities are not a Context.
Related, not the same: ADL's Extension classifies an extension's IRI (a SKOS concept, as an activity type is); this class is the map that carries extension values, keyed by those IRIs.

Not an exact match: ADL's ontology makes xapi:Object disjoint from xapi:Actor (owl:AllDisjointClasses), so an Agent or Group is never an Object there, while xAPI 2.0 lets either be the Object of a Statement (§5.2.2.3) and here Object includes them; and it places Activity Definitions and activity types under xapi:Object, through xapi:Activity. Read as an equivalence, every Agent or Group here would be unsatisfiable.

Broader there: ADL's ontology places xapi:Score under xapi:Result — with rdfs:subClassof, a property RDFS does not define, so no tool reads the triple as an axiom; read as intended, a Result there includes its Score, and here a Score is not a Result. Mapped as broader so that the alignment holds when that triple is corrected.

Broader there: ADL's ontology places the parts of a Statement (Actor, Verb, Object, Context, Result, Authority, Attachments) and the Sub-Statement under xapi:Statement by rdfs:subClassOf, so its instances include them; here a Statement is the record alone, and disjoint from its parts.
ADL declares xapi:Authority an owl:ObjectProperty, as this is; its ontology also uses the IRI as a class (a subclass of xapi:Statement, and one of its disjoint classes).

Not an exact match: ADL's ontology gives xapi:duration the range xsd:duration, which is outside the OWL 2 datatype map, whose values are not strings, and whose lexical space has no weeks (PnW), which xAPI allows; here a duration is the ISO 8601 string the standard prescribes. Read as an equivalence, every duration here would be inconsistent.

Not an exact match: ADL's ontology gives xapi:extensions two domains, xapi:ActivityDefinition and the union of its extension concepts, so whatever has extensions would be an Activity Definition — and so an Activity and an Object, which a Result or a Context cannot be there; and its extensions point at extension concepts, where here they point at the map that carries the values. Read as an equivalence, every Result or Context with extensions would be inconsistent.

Not an exact match: ADL's ontology gives xapi:fileURL the range xsd:string, and here a file URL is an xsd:anyURI (an IRL); OWL 2 keeps the two value spaces apart, so read as an equivalence every file URL here would be inconsistent.
Not an exact match because of kind: ADL declares xapi:member an owl:DatatypeProperty, whose values are literals; a Group's members are Agents, individuals, so here it is an object property.

Not an exact match because of kind: ADL declares xapi:moreInfo an owl:ObjectProperty with the datatype range xsd:anyURI, which OWL 2 DL does not allow; the value is an IRL, a literal, so here it is a datatype property.

Not an exact match: ADL's ontology gives xapi:name two ranges, rdf:langString and xsd:string, whose value spaces are disjoint, so no value is in both; and two domains, one of them xapi:ActivityDefinition, so whatever has a name would be an Activity Definition. Read as an equivalence, every name here — of an Agent, a Group, an Account or an Activity — would be inconsistent.

Not an exact match because of kind: ADL declares xapi:usageType an owl:DatatypeProperty with the class range xapi:AttachmentUsageType, which OWL 2 DL does not allow; a usage type is an IRI naming a concept, so here it is an object property.

Not an exact match because of kind: ADL declares xapi:version an owl:AnnotationProperty, which no class axiom or shape can constrain; here it is a datatype property whose values are xAPI version numbers.
